summary: Anthropic published a case study describing how the Government of Alberta used Claude Code with Opus and Sonnet to scan, remediate and continuously review security vulnerabilities across its government codebases.

practices.reason: The multi-agent scanning pipeline (rules-engine pass then Claude review, 50 parallel agents, red-team/blue-team review agents) is a concrete architecture pattern a team could adapt, though it is reported only from one customer's deployment.
practices.quote: Around 50 agents worked autonomously and in parallel to scan the systems for security vulnerabilities, weaknesses in underlying infrastructure and deployment processes, and gaps in technical documentation.

practices.reason: The red team/blue team agent methodology checking against ~95 security controls is a transferable security evaluation approach, though described only as Alberta's internal process.
practices.quote: A “red team” agent probes an application from the outside, the way an attacker might, and maps how a vulnerability might be exploited. A “blue team” agent then assesses the application’s defenses against an international security standard, and writes a remediation plan that points to the exact files to fix.
